newsitem.title: USA: Envirodyne ups ante in Zapata bid.
newsitem.headline: Envirodyne ups ante in Zapata bid.

text.p: Envirodyne Industries Inc said Wednesday it has formed a special committee to review an acquisition bid by Zapata Corp, which earlier in the day offered $70 million for the rest of the food packaging firm it does not already own.

Envirodyne said it also amended its bylaws to, among other things, require that transactions between Envirodyne and an interested party be reviewed by an independent committee of the board and approved by 80 percent of all directors.

"The board adopted these procedures to protect stockholders from the risks of self-dealing that are inherent in transactions with interested parties," Envirodyne Chairman, President and Chief Executive Edward Gustafson said in a statement.
A spokesman for Zapata did not immediately return a telephone call late Wednesday night.
Zapata, Envirodyne's largest stockholder, stepped up its bid to take control of Envirodyne earlier in the day.
The Houston-based company, co-founded by President George Bush, said the offer was contingent on the election of its board slate at Envirodyne's annual shareholders meeting later this week.

Envirodyne said it formed the special committee so that individuals connected with Zapata who sit on its board do not pose a conflict of interest. In particular, it cited Malcolm and Avram Glazer, who are Zapata's chairman and president, respectively, and who also are members of Envirodyne's board.
In another statement also issued Wednesday, Gustafson said Envirodyne's board is willing to consider any bid it believes is fair to stockholders.
"If the independent board concludes that Zapata's proposal is in the best interests of stockholders, we would obviously proceed with further discussions with Zapata," he added.

"But it makes no sense to begin the process of negotiating a possible acquisition transaction by turning over control of Envirodyne to the very person attempting to buy it, as Zapata's offer requires.
